notation.meaning: edge probability (or expected edge count) between blocks \(r\) and \(s\)

formulas.name: Stochastic block model (Holland, Laskey and Leinhardt 1983)
formulas.where: Pairs are independent given the block assignment. A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

formulas.name: Degree-corrected block model (Karrer and Newman 2011)
formulas.where: Parallel edges and loops are allowed in this multigraph form; \(\theta\) is normalized within each block.

variants.cat_random_sbm: Block model with block probabilities \(\omega\) as in the first formula (the degree-corrected form is the second formula). Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).
variants.gen_sbm: Block model with block probabilities \(\omega\) as in the first formula (the degree-corrected form is the second formula). Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Each \(\omega_{rs}\) must lie in \([0,1]\) in the Bernoulli form.
One block gives G(n,p); a block of one node has no internal pairs.

notation.meaning: number of node pairs: \(\binom n2\) (undirected), \(n(n-1)\) (directed), plus \(n\) if loops are allowed

formulas.name: G(n,m) (Erdos and Renyi 1959)
formulas.latex: \Pr(G)=\binom{N}{m}^{-1}\ \text{for every graph with }m\text{ edges},\qquad 0\le m\le N
formulas.where: Uniform distribution over all graphs with exactly \(m\) edges. A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.cat_gnm: Uniform choice among graphs with \(m\) edges as in the formula. Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).
variants.gen_gnm: Uniform choice among graphs with \(m\) edges as in the formula. Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Not defined for \(m>N\) or \(m<0\).
\(m=0\): the single edgeless graph.
\(m=N\): the single complete graph.
\(n=0\): \(N=0\), only \(m=0\) is valid.
The model is for simple graphs; parallel edges are outside it.

notation.meaning: number of node pairs: \(\binom n2\) (undirected), \(n(n-1)\) (directed), plus \(n\) if loops are allowed

formulas.name: G(n,p) (Gilbert 1959; Erdos and Renyi 1959)
formulas.where: Each of the \(N\) possible edges is present independently with probability \(p\). A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.cat_gnp: Independent edges with probability \(p\) as in the formula. Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).
variants.gen_gnp: Independent edges with probability \(p\) as in the formula. Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Not defined for \(p<0\) or \(p>1\).
\(p=0\) gives the edgeless graph with probability 1.
\(p=1\) gives the complete graph with probability 1.
\(n=0\): the only graph is the empty graph.
With no loops \(N=0\) and the graph has no edges.
Loops are possible only if the model is stated over the \(n\) additional pairs; the original model has none.
The directed form has \(N=n(n-1)\) independent arcs.

formulas.name: Random regular graph (Steger and Wormald 1999; Bollobas 1980)
formulas.latex: \Pr(G)=\Bigl|\{\text{simple graphs on }n\text{ labelled nodes, all degrees }d\}\Bigr|^{-1}
formulas.where: Uniform distribution over labelled \(d\)-regular graphs, which exist exactly when \(nd\) is even and \(d<n\). A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.gen_regular: Uniform \(d\)-regular simple graph. Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Not defined if \(nd\) is odd or \(d\ge n\).
\(d=n-1\) gives the complete graph.
\(d=0\) gives the edgeless graph.

formulas.name: Chung-Lu expected-degree model (Chung and Lu 2002)
formulas.where: With loops allowed, \(\sum_jp_{ij}=w_i\): node \(i\) has expected degree \(w_i\). The condition keeps every \(p_{ij}\le1\). A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.gen_chung_lu: Independent edges with probability \(\rho w_iw_j\). Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).

edge_cases.definition_gives: If \(w_iw_j\rho>1\) the model is not a probability; a tool must cap it (the cap changes the expected degrees).
A node with \(w_i=0\) is isolated with probability 1.
\(p_{ii}=\rho w_i^2\) in the original model; with loops removed the expected degree is below \(w_i\).

configuration_model.note: The stub-matching model is written. The options of the tools (rewiring to remove loops, other degseq methods) are named but not recorded, so only the model itself is defined.

formulas.name: Configuration model (Bollobas 1980; Molloy and Reed 1995; Newman, Strogatz and Watts 2001)
formulas.where: Give node \(i\) \(k_i\) stubs and pair all \(2m\) stubs uniformly at random. The result may contain loops and parallel edges; \(\sum k_i\) must be even. A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.gen_configuration: The stub-matching model above, as a multigraph unless the tool states a simple-graph option (not recorded).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Not defined if \(\sum_ik_i\) is odd.
Expected loops at \(i\): \(\binom{k_i}{2}/(2m-1)\); loops occur with positive probability.
Parallel edges occur with positive probability in the pairing model.
All \(k_i=0\): the edgeless graph.

degree_sequence_realization.note: Havel-Hakimi and the Erdos-Gallai test are written. The bipartite realization (a Gale-Ryser type condition) and the igraph method options are named only.

formulas.name: Graphical test (Erdos and Gallai 1960)
formulas.where: A sequence is the degree sequence of a simple graph exactly when it satisfies this.

formulas.name: Havel-Hakimi step (Havel 1955; Hakimi 1962)
formulas.where: Connect the node of largest degree to the next \(d_1\) largest and recurse; the realization is deterministic once the tie order among equal degrees is fixed.

variants.cat_generator_hakimi_havel: Realization by the Havel-Hakimi recursion above.
variants.gen_degree_realization: Realization of a degree sequence; the choice of which node to connect first (the tool's method option) changes the graph and is not recorded here.

edge_cases.definition_gives: Not defined (no simple graph) for a sequence that violates the Erdos-Gallai condition or has odd sum.
Among equal degrees the realized graph depends on the order used by the algorithm.

formulas.name: Static model (Goh, Kahng and Kim 2001)
formulas.latex: P_i=\frac{f_i}{\sum_jf_j},\quad f_i=i^{-\mu}\ \ (0\le\mu<1);\ \ \text{repeat }L\text{ times: pick }i\ne j\text{ with probabilities }P_i,P_j\text{, add the edge if absent}
formulas.where: Node fitness fixed in advance gives a power-law degree tail of exponent \(1+1/\mu\). A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.gen_static_fitness: Fitness-weighted edge placement; with fitness \(i^{-\mu}\) it is the static power-law model.

formulas.name: LFR benchmark (Lancichinetti, Fortunato and Radicchi 2008)

formulas.where: Degrees and community sizes follow power laws; \(\mu\) controls how well communities are separated. A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

formulas.latex: \text{first edge by preferential attachment; each further edge: with probability }p\text{ to a random neighbour of the last target, otherwise preferential attachment}
formulas.where: Adding triad formation to linear attachment raises clustering while keeping the power-law degree tail. A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

notation.meaning: number of edges added with each new node

formulas.name: Barabasi-Albert growth (Barabasi and Albert 1999)
formulas.where: At each step a new node is added with \(m\le m_0\) edges to distinct existing nodes chosen with probability \(\Pi(i)\). The result depends on the initial graph and the random generator. A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.gen_preferential: Linear attachment by degree as in the formula; direction, initial graph and exponent options are not recorded.
variants.cat_pa: Preferential attachment; the options are not recorded.
variants.cat_age_pa: Attachment with an age term in addition to degree; the age function is not recorded here.

edge_cases.definition_gives: Needs \(m\le m_0\) so that \(m\) distinct targets exist.
A starting single node has degree 0, so \(\Pi\) is 0/0; implementations must give initial nodes an offset or a seed graph.

formulas.name: R-MAT (Chakrabarti, Zhan and Faloutsos 2004)
formulas.latex: \Pr\bigl(\text{edge in quadrant }q\bigr)=a,b,c,d\ \text{ for top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right; recurse }s\text{ times}
formulas.where: Each edge is placed by choosing a quadrant of the adjacency matrix with these probabilities and recursing into it until a single cell remains; repeated cells give parallel edges. notation.meaning: branching factor and height of a balanced tree

formulas.name: Named graphs (Harary 1969)
formulas.latex: K_n:\ i\sim j\ \forall i\ne j;\ \ P_n:\ i\sim i{+}1;\ \ C_n:\ P_n\ \text{plus}\ (n{-}1)\sim0;\ \ S_n:\ 0\sim i\ (i\ge1);\ \ W_n:\ C_{n-1}\ \text{plus a hub};\ \ Q_d:\ \{0,1\}^d,\ x\sim y\iff\text{they differ in one bit}
formulas.where: Complete, path, cycle, star, wheel and hypercube. \(Q_0\) has \(2^0=1\) node. The ladder is \(P_n\times K_2\), the grid \(P_a\times P_b\), the balanced tree has \(\sum_{i=0}^h r^i\) nodes, the complete bipartite graph \(K_{a,b}\) joins every node of one part to every node of the other.

variants.deterministic_generators: All generators above, with the node numbering of the tool; the numbering of grids, hypercubes and trees follows each tool's convention.

edge_cases.definition_gives: \(K_0\), \(P_0\), \(S_0\) have no nodes; \(Q_0=K_1\) has one node, since \(2^0=1\).

networkx.behaviour: nx.hypercube_graph(0) returns the null graph, while the reference and the definition give Q_0 = K_1 (one node). Convention, on the null graph only.

edge_cases.definition_gives: \(K_1\), \(P_1\), \(C_1\) (a single node, a loop only if loops are admitted) and \(S_1\) are one node.
\(C_n\) needs \(n\ge3\) to be simple; \(W_n\) needs \(n\ge4\).
Directed versions orient path and cycle edges along increasing index; the complete digraph has all \(n(n-1)\) arcs.

swap_contract.note: Only the degree-preserving double edge swap is written (Maslov and Sneppen 2002). The windowed connected swap of NetworkX and the directed three-edge swap are named in the sources and their rules are not written here; the checked contract is stated as a property of the result.

formulas.name: Double edge swap (Maslov and Sneppen 2002)
formulas.where: Two edges are chosen at random and their endpoints exchanged; every degree is unchanged. Repeated swaps sample graphs with the same degree sequence. A swap that would create a loop or a duplicate edge is rejected. A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

formulas.name: Contract of a result
formulas.latex: \deg_{E'}(v)=\deg_E(v)\ \forall v,\qquad |E'|=|E|,\qquad E'\ \text{simple}\ (\text{and connected for the connected variant})
formulas.where: Properties every rewired edge list \(E'\) must satisfy; two tools can be compared through this contract, not draw by draw, because their random generators differ.

variants.swap_contract: Rewired edge list and number of swaps kept, for the double swap, the connectivity-preserving swap, or the directed swap; the contract above holds for each.

edge_cases.definition_gives: Every double swap on a star creates a loop or duplicate, so no swap is possible; a procedure that keeps drawing never stops unless it has a limit.

networkx.behaviour: lattice_reference and random_reference (seed 7) on a star: every draw is rejected and NetworkX redraws forever; the reference stops each round after 100(m+1) rejected draws.

edge_cases.definition_gives: Fewer than four nodes or two edges: no swap exists.
The connectivity-preserving swap is not defined for a disconnected input.
The simple-graph definition has no parallel edges; the result must not have any.
Swaps creating loops are rejected; the input is a simple graph.
For directed graphs the swap keeps in- and out-degrees (the directed three-edge swap is not written here).

formulas.name: Random geometric graph (Penrose 2003)
formulas.where: Nodes are random points, an edge joins points within distance \(r\). A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.gen_geometric: Connect points within radius \(r\); the norm and the boundary (torus or not) are options not recorded. Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Not defined for \(r<0\).
\(r\) below the smallest distance gives no edges.
\(r\) at least the largest distance gives the complete graph.
Pairs at distance exactly \(r\) are included (non-strict inequality in the definition).

notation.meaning: each node joined to its \(k\) nearest ring neighbours (\(k\) even)

formulas.name: Watts-Strogatz model (Watts and Strogatz 1998)
formulas.latex: \text{ring lattice }C_n^{k};\ \ \text{each edge }(i,i{+}j),\,j\le k/2,\ \text{is rewired with probability }p\text{ to a uniformly chosen new target}
formulas.where: Targets that would create a loop or a duplicate edge are not allowed; \(p=0\) leaves the lattice, \(p=1\) is close to a random graph. Defined for even \(k<n\). A generator returns a random sample, so a result is reproducible only for a fixed seed and random generator; tools use different generators.

variants.gen_small_world: Ring lattice with rewiring probability \(p\) (Watts-Strogatz). Which options this function offers is not recorded (documented by name only).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Needs even \(k\) with \(k<n\) and \(0\le p\le1\).
\(k=0\) gives no edges.
\(k=n-1\) leaves no room to rewire: the complete graph.
